MARKET OVERVIEW

1. What is the Current Market Regime?
RISK-ON: normal volatility at 33.0% and broad participation, with all 8/8 sectors positive on the week. Breadth is supportive, though several sectors remain below their monthly levels.

2. Which sectors are leading?
Transportation leads at +21.49% for the week and +5.09% for the month: THYAO (1W: +23.55% | 1M: +4.54%) ABOVE TREND. Technology & Telecom (+16.89% weekly) and Banking & Finance (+12.17%) follow; KONTR (1W: +46.45% | 1M: +29.47%) is ABOVE TREND.

3. Which sectors are lagging?
Retail & Food (+5.62% weekly) is the weakest sector, with a negative monthly return of 7.48%; SOKM (1W: -6.58% | 1M: -11.93%) is BELOW TREND. Heavy Industry and Energy & Chemicals also remain negative over the month, down 11.74% and 13.46%, respectively.

STOCK PERFORMANCE

4. Top Performing Stocks?
The top five by weekly return are KONTR (1W: +46.45% | 1M: +29.47%) ABOVE TREND, THYAO (1W: +23.55% | 1M: +4.54%) ABOVE TREND, PGSUS (1W: +23.13% | 1M: +3.74%) ABOVE TREND, TRMET (1W: +18.98% | 1M: -11.54%) RECOVERY, and TAVHL (1W: +17.80% | 1M: +6.99%) ABOVE TREND.

5. Worst Performing Stocks?
Weak monthly performers include TKFEN (1W: -1.25% | 1M: -29.48%) BELOW TREND, GUBRF (1W: +15.58% | 1M: -26.28%) RECOVERY, PETKM (1W: +0.55% | 1M: -18.76%) RECOVERY, and TCELL (1W: -0.11% | 1M: -9.46%) BELOW TREND. SOKM (1W: -6.58% | 1M: -11.93%) is also BELOW TREND, and posted the weakest weekly return.

6. Momentum Stocks?
Weekly momentum is strongest in KONTR (1W: +46.45% | 1M: +29.47%) ABOVE TREND, THYAO (1W: +23.55% | 1M: +4.54%) ABOVE TREND, and PGSUS (1W: +23.13% | 1M: +3.74%) ABOVE TREND. TRMET (1W: +18.98% | 1M: -11.54%) RECOVERY and TRALT (1W: +17.64% | 1M: -7.74%) RECOVERY are sharp bounces, but remain below monthly levels.

SECTOR OUTLOOK

7. Banking Sector Outlook?
Banking & Finance is strong on both timeframes, averaging +12.17% weekly and +1.43% monthly. GARAN (1W: +15.26% | 1M: +11.09%) and ISCTR (1W: +14.08% | 1M: +2.47%) are ABOVE TREND; AKBNK (1W: +12.73% | 1M: -0.87%) is in RECOVERY.

8. Industrial Sector Outlook?
Heavy Industry gained 6.65% on the week but remains down 11.74% over the month. TOASO (1W: +15.06% | 1M: -7.43%) and FROTO (1W: +11.76% | 1M: -0.95%) are in RECOVERY, while ASELS (1W: -4.39% | 1M: -4.87%) is BELOW TREND.

9. Energy & Chemicals Outlook?
The sector rose 9.54% weekly but remains down 13.46% monthly, with the quant screen disqualifying the group on its two-week return. TRMET (1W: +18.98% | 1M: -11.54%) and GUBRF (1W: +15.58% | 1M: -26.28%) are in RECOVERY; TUPRS (1W: -1.75% | 1M: -11.13%) is BELOW TREND.

PORTFOLIO STRATEGY

10. Portfolio Recommendation?
Maintain a constructive, selective risk-on stance: favor confirmed leaders in transportation, technology and banking, while using staged entries after outsized weekly rallies. Keep risk controls tight in sectors with negative monthly returns; breadth is strong, but it does not yet confirm a broad monthly recovery.

NEXT WEEK OUTLOOK

11. Stocks to Watch Next Week?
Monitor KONTR (1W: +46.45% | 1M: +29.47%) ABOVE TREND for follow-through, and THYAO (1W: +23.55% | 1M: +4.54%) and PGSUS (1W: +23.13% | 1M: +3.74%), both ABOVE TREND, for continuation. GARAN (1W: +15.26% | 1M: +11.09%) ABOVE TREND offers a banking confirmation, while GUBRF (1W: +15.58% | 1M: -26.28%) RECOVERY remains a high-volatility rebound watch.

12. Sectors to Watch Next Week?
Transportation is the clearest leader, with positive weekly and monthly returns. Track Technology & Telecom and Banking & Finance for continued leadership, while watching whether Energy & Chemicals can extend its weekly bounce despite a deeply negative monthly return.

13. Key Levels & Triggers?
No XU100 price levels were provided, so specific support and resistance levels cannot be stated. Key triggers are a hold in market breadth at or above 5/8 positive sectors, volatility staying below 40%, and sustained monthly improvement in currently lagging sectors.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

BIST 50 is RISK-ON, supported by normal volatility of 33.0% and positive weekly returns across all eight sectors. Transportation, technology and banks lead, while energy and heavy industry show weekly rebounds against negative monthly trends; monitor follow-through and manage exposure to sharp rallies.
